transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-04-15 08:00 PT | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CSM) — Bluefjord: Oliver Grant (Head of Data), Tanya Li (Security Eng), Rajiv Menon (Platform), Sofia Cortez (Privacy)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — run through the retention numbers we applied for the pilot, SSO test cadence, audit log export, and then SOC2 artifacts. anything to add?
[00:12] Oliver Grant: that works. curious mostly about retention TTLs — we have a tight 90 day window for PII, but some logs we want 1 year.
[00:20] Diego Ramos: yeah we built the pilot with token-level retention toggles; default is 365 but we can override per-route. for the pilot, we suggested 90 for user content and 365 for system logs.
[00:30] Tanya Li: can you explain where the audit logs are stored and how we pull them? we need event-level detail for our SIEM.
[00:40] Diego Ramos: audit logs are emitted to a customer-owned S3 or to the Redcloud audit API. for Bluefjord we recommended S3 export with SSE-KMS, and we can push daily manifests. the schema includes request id, model, input hash, top-level token counts, user id (if supplied), and action type. we can add extra fields if you need them.
[01:05] Rajiv Menon: is there a way to reduce PII stored in the logs? e.g. strip prompt content while keeping metadata?
[01:12] Diego Ramos: yes — we support redaction hooks that drop or hash prompt text before logging. that runs in the private control plane or in-hosted masking layer, depending on deployment. for hosted pilot we can enable redaction and keep hashed prompts instead.
[01:35] Sofia Cortez: good — legal will want to see an audit trail proving redaction and retention enforcement.
[01:40] Maya Patel: on that note, we will hand over a SOC2 snapshot and a short how-to on audit exports after this call. that should address some of the evidence items.
[01:50] Tanya Li: for SSO, we run SAML with SCIM for groups. will Redwood support group sync and role mapping?
[02:00] Diego Ramos: yes. we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. role mapping is configurable in the console; by default we map groups to RBAC templates but you can send a custom mapping file. we can run a test in staging.
[02:15] Oliver Grant: what about session timeouts and token revocation? if someone leaves, we need immediate revocation.
[02:22] Diego Ramos: session tokens are short lived — default 1 hour — and we support immediate revocation via an admin API that invalidates sessions and keys. for the pilot we can lower TTL to 15 minutes if you want more aggressive short-lived sessions.
[02:35] Maya Patel: quick check — Tanya, are you ok to run the SSO test next week?
[02:40] Tanya Li: yes, Tuesday morning works. I'll want Diego on the call for SCIM troubleshooting.
[02:46] Diego Ramos: noted. we'll spin up a test SP and share the SAML metadata.
[02:50] Maya Patel: moving to retention: during pilot we propose setting conversation content TTL to 90 days and embeddings to 365, with audit log retention at 730 for compliance review. thoughts?
[03:05] Rajiv Menon: 730 for logs is fine but legal will push back unless we can show access controls.
[03:10] Sofia Cortez: can we restrict access to the bucket with RBAC and require KMS decrypt approvals?
[03:15] Diego Ramos: yes — S3 bucket access via IAM policies scoped down, and KMS keys in a customer-owned key alias can enforce decrypt permissions. we support HSM-backed KMS via marketplace integrations.
[03:30] Oliver Grant: what's the expected size of the audit export? rough numbers per 10k requests?
[03:36] Diego Ramos: rough estimate — about 4–6 KB per request for the audit record (metadata only); if you include prompt snapshots it goes up. we can give you a sample export for your 10k/day workload to size S3.
[03:50] Maya Patel: action item — Rajiv to send a sample of expected monthly traffic so Diego can run sizing.
[03:55] Rajiv Menon: I'll get that today.
[04:00] Tanya Li: SOC2 — we want to see the Type II report and key control descriptions, plus encryption at rest and in transit. also logs for admin actions.
[04:12] Maya Patel: we'll share the SOC2 snapshot and the control matrix. encryption: TLS in transit, AES-256 for data at rest, and customer-managed KMS available. admin action logs are included in the audit export.
[04:25] Tanya Li: do you provide attestations for supporting sub processors? we need a list for our supplier risk team.
[04:30] Priya Shah: yes we'll send a current subprocessor list with the security pack.
[04:35] Oliver Grant: one more — we plan to run a small spike to check latency for private deployment. who owns that?
[04:42] Diego Ramos: Redwood SE will run the initial benchmark with your sample workload in staging; if you move to Private we'll run the on-prem/ VPC performance profiler.
[04:52] Maya Patel: recap — Redwood sends SOC2 and security pack by Friday, Diego enables SAML staging tenant and shares metadata, Rajiv provides sample traffic, and we schedule SSO test on Tue 2026-04-20.
[05:05] Tanya Li: agreed. also please include a short doc on redaction hooks so legal can review.
[05:10] Maya Patel: will do. any blockers?
[05:12] Oliver Grant: none on our side — sounds good.
[05:15] Maya Patel: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for the SSO test.

Meeting ended at 08:42 PT
